title: Keycloak OIDC Integration
description:
## Objective
Add Keycloak as an OAuth/OIDC identity provider to Plane, enabling enterprise SSO via OpenID Connect Authorization Code Flow.

## Scope
- Backend: KeycloakOAuthProvider, views (app + space), URL routes, error codes, instance config, Account model update, migration
- Frontend: TypeScript types, OAuth button in web + space apps, admin configuration UI
- Config: Instance-level Keycloak settings (host, realm, client_id, client_secret, enable flag, sync flag)

## Non-Goals
- Generic OIDC provider support (Keycloak-specific only)
- SAML support
- Keycloak admin API integration
- Multi-realm support
- Group/role mapping
- Logout propagation

## Key Decisions
- D1: Use userinfo endpoint instead of id_token decoding (consistent with other providers)
- D2: Keycloak-specific provider, not generic OIDC
- D3: Single realm per instance
- D4: Callback URLs: `/auth/keycloak/callback/` (app), `/auth/spaces/keycloak/callback/` (space)
- D5: Error codes: 5113 (KEYCLOAK_NOT_CONFIGURED), 5124 (KEYCLOAK_OAUTH_PROVIDER_ERROR)
- D6: Config: IS_KEYCLOAK_ENABLED, ENABLE_KEYCLOAK_SYNC naming pattern
- D7: Ignore email_verified claim (consistent with other providers)

## Success Criteria
- End-to-end login flow works: click "Sign in with Keycloak" → Keycloak redirect → authenticate → redirect back with active session
- Admin can enable/disable Keycloak and configure credentials from admin UI
- Existing OAuth providers remain unaffected
- No new dependencies introduced
- `pnpm check` and Django server start without errors
close_reason: All children closed: Keycloak OIDC integration complete

title: Error Codes & OAuth Adapter Update
description:
## Objective
Register two Keycloak-specific error codes and update the OAuth adapter's error mapping so Keycloak auth errors return the correct error code instead of the generic fallback.

## Context
Plane's OAuth flow uses provider-specific error codes. Without this, Keycloak errors would fall through to the default `OAUTH_NOT_CONFIGURED` (5104) which is misleading — it's an instance-level code, not a provider-level one.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Add 2 error codes to `apps/api/plane/authentication/adapter/error.py`
- Add `"keycloak"` case to `authentication_error_code()` in `apps/api/plane/authentication/adapter/oauth.py`

**Out of scope:**
- Any changes to other providers' error codes
- Frontend error handling (separate bead)

## Components Touched
- `apps/api/plane/authentication/adapter/error.py` — add error code definitions
- `apps/api/plane/authentication/adapter/oauth.py` — add case to `authentication_error_code()` method

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
None — this is foundation work.

## Important Assumptions and Constraints
- Error code 5113 for `KEYCLOAK_NOT_CONFIGURED` (fits in "not configured" range 5104-5112)
- Error code 5124 for `KEYCLOAK_OAUTH_PROVIDER_ERROR` (extends "provider error" range 5115-5123)
- These exact values must be used — they are referenced by other beads
- Follow the exact pattern of existing error code definitions (e.g., GITEA codes)

## Risks / Gotchas
- Error code values must be unique. Verify current highest codes before adding.
- The `authentication_error_code()` mapping is critical — missing it causes all Keycloak token/userinfo errors to report code 5104 instead of 5124.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `KEYCLOAK_NOT_CONFIGURED = 5113` exists in `error.py`
- `KEYCLOAK_OAUTH_PROVIDER_ERROR = 5124` exists in `error.py`
- `authentication_error_code()` in `oauth.py` returns `"KEYCLOAK_OAUTH_PROVIDER_ERROR"` when `self.provider == "keycloak"`
- Python syntax valid (no import errors)
- Existing error codes unchanged
close_reason: Implemented: Added KEYCLOAK_NOT_CONFIGURED=5113 and KEYCLOAK_OAUTH_PROVIDER_ERROR=5124 error codes; added keycloak case to authentication_error_code() method

title: KeycloakOAuthProvider Class
description:
## Objective
Create the KeycloakOAuthProvider class that handles Keycloak OIDC token exchange and user info retrieval.

## Context
Each OAuth provider in Plane has a provider class extending OauthAdapter. The provider is instantiated by views with a request + code, then `authenticate()` is called (inherited from OauthAdapter). The provider class handles: config fetching, token exchange, and user data retrieval.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Create `apps/api/plane/authentication/provider/oauth/keycloak.py`
- Implement `KeycloakOAuthProvider` class extending `OauthAdapter`

**Out of scope:**
- Views that use this provider (separate beads 2.2, 2.5)
- Error code definitions (separate bead 1.1)

## Components Touched
- `apps/api/plane/authentication/provider/oauth/keycloak.py` (NEW)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Error Codes (xplane-4ks.1.1) — uses KEYCLOAK_NOT_CONFIGURED
- Instance Config (xplane-epi) — reads config variables

## Important Assumptions and Constraints
- **Primary template:** Follow `apps/api/plane/authentication/provider/oauth/gitea.py` exactly
- **Class structure:**
  - `__init__(self, request, code=None, callback=None)`: Fetch config via `get_configuration_value`, validate host+realm, build `token_url` and `userinfo_url`, call `super().__init__()`
  - `set_token_data(self)`: Call `self.get_user_token(data=..., headers=...)`, extract access_token and compute expiry
  - `set_user_data(self)`: Call userinfo endpoint with Bearer token, extract email/name/avatar
  - `create_update_account(self)`: Inherited from OauthAdapter (no override needed)
- **Keycloak URLs:**
  - Token URL: `{host}/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token`
  - Userinfo URL: `{host}/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/userinfo`
  - Auth URL: `{host}/realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth`
- **Config keys read:** IS_KEYCLOAK_ENABLED, KEYCLOAK_HOST, KEYCLOAK_REALM, KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID, KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET
- **Super init args:** `provider='keycloak', request=request, self.token_url, self.userinfo_url, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, code, callback`
- **Redirect URI:** Built from `base_host(request=request, is_app=True)` + `/auth/keycloak/callback/` (or passed in by views)
- **Scope:** `openid email profile`
- **Error on missing config:** Raise `AuthenticationException` with `KEYCLOAK_NOT_CONFIGURED` (error code 5113) and status 400

## Acceptance Criteria
- Class inherits from OauthAdapter
- Config fetched and validated in __init__
- Token exchange works via standard OAuth2 code flow
- User data extracted from userinfo endpoint (email, first_name, last_name)
- AuthenticationException raised if config missing
- Python syntax valid
- No new pip dependencies

comments.author: cuongnt3
comments.text: [POLISH] CORRECTION: The redirect_uri is NOT built from base_host(). Follow the gitea.py pattern exactly: redirect_uri = f"{'https' if request.is_secure() else 'http'}://{request.get_host()}/auth/keycloak/callback/". The base_host() function is only used by views for post-auth redirects, not by the provider for OAuth callback URIs.

title: App Views (Initiate + Callback)
description:
## Objective
Create Django views for the Keycloak OAuth initiate and callback endpoints for the main web app.

## Context
Plane's OAuth flow starts with an initiate view (redirects user to provider) and a callback view (processes the redirect back with auth code). App views use `base_host(request=request, is_app=True)` and pass `callback=post_user_auth_workflow` to the provider.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Create `apps/api/plane/authentication/views/app/keycloak.py`
- Implement `KeycloakOauthInitiateEndpoint` (GET → redirect to Keycloak)
- Implement `KeycloakCallbackEndpoint` (GET → process callback, create session)

**Out of scope:**
- Space views (separate bead)
- URL routing (separate bead)
- Provider class (separate bead — this bead uses it)

## Components Touched
- `apps/api/plane/authentication/views/app/keycloak.py` (NEW)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- KeycloakOAuthProvider (xplane-4ks.2.1) — views instantiate this provider
- Error Codes (xplane-4ks.1.1) — views reference error codes for error handling

## Important Assumptions and Constraints
- **Primary template:** Follow `apps/api/plane/authentication/views/app/gitlab.py` exactly for structure
- App views use `base_host(request=request, is_app=True)` (NOT `is_space=True`)
- Callback view passes `callback=post_user_auth_workflow` to provider constructor
- Initiate view: generates state token, builds auth URL, redirects
- Callback view: validates state, creates provider with auth code, calls `authenticate()`, sets session, redirects to app
- Error handling: catch exceptions, redirect to error page with appropriate error code
- Use `KEYCLOAK_OAUTH_PROVIDER_ERROR` for auth failures, `KEYCLOAK_NOT_CONFIGURED` for missing config

## Acceptance Criteria
- Initiate endpoint redirects to correct Keycloak auth URL with `client_id`, `scope=openid email profile`, `state`, `redirect_uri`
- Callback endpoint exchanges code for tokens and creates session
- Errors redirect to error page with correct error codes
- Follows GitLab app view pattern exactly
- Python syntax valid

title: URL Routing & View Exports
description:
## Objective
Wire up URL patterns for all four Keycloak endpoints and add view imports to the views package `__init__.py`.

## Context
Plane's authentication URL routing is in `apps/api/plane/authentication/urls.py`. Views must be importable from the views package. This bead connects the views (created in prior beads) to the URL dispatcher.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Add 4 URL patterns to `apps/api/plane/authentication/urls.py`:
  1. `auth/keycloak/` → `KeycloakOauthInitiateEndpoint` (app initiate)
  2. `auth/keycloak/callback/` → `KeycloakCallbackEndpoint` (app callback)
  3. `auth/spaces/keycloak/` → `KeycloakOauthSpaceInitiateEndpoint` (space initiate)
  4. `auth/spaces/keycloak/callback/` → `KeycloakCallbackSpaceEndpoint` (space callback)
- Update `apps/api/plane/authentication/views/__init__.py` to export new view classes

**Out of scope:**
- View implementations (separate beads)

## Components Touched
- `apps/api/plane/authentication/urls.py`
- `apps/api/plane/authentication/views/__init__.py`

**NOTE:** There are NO `views/app/__init__.py` or `views/space/__init__.py` files. The main `views/__init__.py` imports directly from submodules:
```python
from .app.keycloak import KeycloakOauthInitiateEndpoint, KeycloakCallbackEndpoint
from .space.keycloak import KeycloakOauthSpaceInitiateEndpoint, KeycloakCallbackSpaceEndpoint
```

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- App Views (xplane-4ks.2.2) — must exist before routing can import them
- Space Views (xplane-4ks.2.5) — must exist before routing can import them

## Important Assumptions and Constraints
- URL patterns follow existing convention: `auth/<provider>/` and `auth/<provider>/callback/` for app, `auth/spaces/<provider>/` and `auth/spaces/<provider>/callback/` for space
- Follow exact pattern of existing GitLab/Gitea URL entries
- View class names: `KeycloakOauthInitiateEndpoint`, `KeycloakCallbackEndpoint`, `KeycloakOauthSpaceInitiateEndpoint`, `KeycloakCallbackSpaceEndpoint`

## Acceptance Criteria
- All 4 URL patterns registered
- Views importable from `plane.authentication.views`
- Django URL resolution works (no import errors on server start)
- URL pattern names follow existing convention
- Existing URL patterns unchanged

title: Space Views (Initiate + Callback)
description:
## Objective
Create Django views for the Keycloak OAuth initiate and callback endpoints for the Space app.

## Context
Space views differ from app views in three critical ways: (1) use `is_space=True` in `base_host(request, is_space=True)`, (2) do NOT pass `callback=post_user_auth_workflow` to the provider — space callbacks omit the post-auth workflow, (3) use `validate_next_path` and `get_allowed_hosts` for redirect validation.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Create `apps/api/plane/authentication/views/space/keycloak.py`
- Implement `KeycloakOauthSpaceInitiateEndpoint` (GET → redirect to Keycloak)
- Implement `KeycloakCallbackSpaceEndpoint` (GET → process callback, create session)

**Out of scope:**
- App views (separate bead)
- URL routing (separate bead)

## Components Touched
- `apps/api/plane/authentication/views/space/keycloak.py` (NEW)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- KeycloakOAuthProvider (xplane-4ks.2.1) — views instantiate this provider
- Error Codes (xplane-4ks.1.1) — views reference error codes

## Important Assumptions and Constraints
- **Primary template:** Follow `apps/api/plane/authentication/views/space/gitea.py` (NOT the app views)
- **Key differences from app views:**
  1. `base_host(request, is_space=True)` — must pass `is_space=True`
  2. Do NOT pass `callback=post_user_auth_workflow` — space omits this
  3. Use `validate_next_path` and `get_allowed_hosts` for redirect validation
- Error handling same as app views but redirect target may differ

## Risks / Gotchas
- Easy mistake: copy-pasting from app views and forgetting `is_space=True` or including `post_user_auth_workflow`. This would break space auth flow.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Space initiate endpoint redirects to correct Keycloak auth URL
- Space callback endpoint uses `is_space=True` in `base_host()`
- Space callback does NOT use `post_user_auth_workflow`
- Space callback uses `validate_next_path` and `get_allowed_hosts`
- Follows Gitea space view pattern exactly
- Python syntax valid

title: Admin Config Page & Form
description:
## Objective
Build the Keycloak configuration page and form for the admin app, allowing admins to enter Keycloak connection details.

## Context
Each OAuth provider has a dedicated admin config page with a form. The Keycloak form has one extra field compared to GitLab: "Realm". The form saves via the existing generic `InstanceConfigurationEndpoint`.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Create `keycloak/page.tsx` — config page wrapper
- Create `keycloak/form.tsx` — configuration form component
- Form fields: Host, Realm, Client ID, Client Secret, Sync toggle, Callback URL display

**Out of scope:**
- Toggle component (separate bead)
- Backend config endpoint (already exists as generic endpoint)

## Components Touched
- New page and form files in admin app auth directory (follow existing provider page patterns)

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
- Frontend Types (xplane-4ks.1.4) — needs `TInstanceKeycloakAuthenticationConfigurationKeys`
- Admin Hooks & Routes (xplane-4ks.3.3) — route must exist to navigate to this page

## Important Assumptions and Constraints
- **Primary template:** Follow `apps/admin/app/(all)/(dashboard)/authentication/gitea/form.tsx` pattern exactly
- Uses `react-hook-form` for form state
- Imports `IFormattedInstanceConfiguration` from `@plane/types`
- Saves via `useInstance().updateInstanceConfigurations(payload)` which calls `PATCH /api/instances/configurations/`
- No custom backend handler needed — uses existing generic `InstanceConfigurationEndpoint`
- Form fields and their config keys:
  - Host → `KEYCLOAK_HOST`
  - Realm → `KEYCLOAK_REALM` (unique to Keycloak — extra field vs GitLab)
  - Client ID → `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID`
  - Client Secret → `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET`
  - Sync toggle → `ENABLE_KEYCLOAK_SYNC`
- Callback URL display: show `{instance_url}/auth/keycloak/callback/` as read-only for admin to copy-paste into Keycloak client config
- Layout should match GitLab form pattern with the Realm field added

## Risks / Gotchas
- The form is the largest single frontend component (~230 lines). It's a clone-and-modify from GitLab form, so complexity is manageable.
- Must handle `KEYCLOAK_REALM` field which no other provider has — needs an appropriate label and help text.

## Acceptance Criteria
- Page renders at the admin keycloak auth route
- Form displays all 5 config fields (Host, Realm, Client ID, Client Secret, Sync)
- Callback URL is displayed read-only
- Save persists all values via `updateInstanceConfigurations`
- Client Secret field is masked/password type
- `pnpm check:types` passes
- Form validates required fields before save
- Layout matches existing provider config forms

title: Instance Configuration Variables (Keycloak)
description:
## Objective
Define Keycloak config variables and expose the `is_keycloak_enabled` flag via the instance API endpoint.

## Context
Plane stores OAuth provider configuration in `InstanceConfiguration` (database). Each provider has config variables seeded on startup and an enable flag exposed via the instance API. The admin UI and frontend apps read `is_keycloak_enabled` to decide whether to show the Keycloak login button.

## Scope
**In scope:**
- Add `keycloak_config_variables` list to `apps/api/plane/utils/instance_config_variables/core.py`
- Append `keycloak_config_variables` to `core_config_variables`
- Update `InstanceEndpoint.get()` in `apps/api/plane/license/api/views/instance.py` (3 changes)

**Out of scope:**
- Admin UI for editing these config values (separate bead)
- Provider class that reads these values (separate bead)

## Components Touched
- `apps/api/plane/utils/instance_config_variables/core.py` — add config variable definitions
- `apps/api/plane/license/api/views/instance.py` — expose `is_keycloak_enabled` in API response

## Dependencies / Prerequisites
None — this is foundation work.

## Important Assumptions and Constraints
- 6 config keys: `IS_KEYCLOAK_ENABLED`, `KEYCLOAK_HOST`, `KEYCLOAK_REALM`, `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID`, `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET`, `ENABLE_KEYCLOAK_SYNC`
- `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET` must have `is_encrypted: True`
- `IS_KEYCLOAK_ENABLED` is seeded (following Gitea's pattern, not Google/GitHub/GitLab which don't seed their enable flags)
- Initial values come from environment variables via `os.environ.get()`
- Follow exact pattern of `gitea_config_variables` in `core.py`

### InstanceEndpoint.get() changes (3 places):
1. Add `{"key": "IS_KEYCLOAK_ENABLED", "default": os.environ.get("IS_KEYCLOAK_ENABLED", "0")}` to the `get_configuration_value()` list
2. Add `IS_KEYCLOAK_ENABLED` to the positional tuple destructuring (append as last position — **order must match the list of dicts**)
3. Add `data["is_keycloak_enabled"] = IS_KEYCLOAK_ENABLED == "1"` to the data dict

**Critical:** Read the current `get_configuration_value()` call before editing. Count existing entries and append to both the list and tuple in the same position. A mismatch silently assigns wrong values.

## Risks / Gotchas
- The tuple destructuring in `InstanceEndpoint.get()` is position-sensitive. Adding to the list without updating the tuple (or vice versa) silently assigns wrong config values to wrong variables.
- Must verify the current count of entries before appending.

## Acceptance Criteria
- `keycloak_config_variables` list defined with all 6 keys
- `KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_SECRET` has `is_encrypted: True`
- `keycloak_config_variables` included in `core_config_variables`
- `InstanceEndpoint.get()` returns `is_keycloak_enabled` boolean in response
- Python syntax valid
- Existing config variables unchanged
